title: Linux System Call Tables by Architecture · syscall.sh
excerpt: The Linux syscall table for 27 architectures: every system call number, argument and register, with a table per architecture, from Linux 3.3 to 7.3.
content_html:
Every Linux syscall table in one place, grouped by architecture: system calls for 27 architectures with their numbers, arguments and registers, from Linux 3.3 to 7.3.

Architectures

  • x64 x86_64 369 syscalls · since 3.3
  • x86 i386, 32 bit x86 441 syscalls · since 3.3
  • arm64 AArch64 326 syscalls · since 3.7
  • arm ARM EABI, 32 bit 426 syscalls · since 4.10
  • riscv64 RISC-V, 64 bit 327 syscalls · since 4.15
  • ia32 IA-32 compat on x86_64 439 syscalls · since 3.3
  • x32 x32 ABI on x86_64 369 syscalls · since 3.4
  • loongarch64 LoongArch, 64 bit 323 syscalls · since 5.19
  • ppc64 PowerPC, 64 bit 383 syscalls · since 5.0
  • ppc PowerPC, 32 bit 425 syscalls · since 5.0
  • s390x IBM Z 378 syscalls · since 4.16
  • mips64 MIPS n64 ABI 363 syscalls · since 5.0
  • mipsn32 MIPS n32 ABI 387 syscalls · since 5.0
  • mipso32 MIPS o32 ABI 413 syscalls · since 5.0
  • alpha DEC Alpha 403 syscalls · since 5.0
  • arc Synopsys ARC 350 syscalls · since 3.9
  • csky C-SKY 346 syscalls · since 4.20
  • hexagon Qualcomm Hexagon 345 syscalls · since 3.7
  • m68k Motorola 68000 435 syscalls · since 5.0
  • microblaze Xilinx MicroBlaze 423 syscalls · since 5.0
  • nios2 Intel Nios II 346 syscalls · since 3.19
  • openrisc OpenRISC 346 syscalls · since 3.7
  • parisc HP PA-RISC 404 syscalls · since 5.0
  • sh SuperH 433 syscalls · since 5.0
  • sparc SPARC, 32 bit 434 syscalls · since 5.0
  • sparc64 SPARC, 64 bit 399 syscalls · since 5.0
  • xtensa Tensilica Xtensa 388 syscalls · since 5.0

Every architecture's table, with the full history of when each syscall appeared and when it was dropped, is also a plain JSON file at /<arch>/syscalls.json, for example /x64/syscalls.json.

Calling conventions

Number in NR, arguments in ARG0 to ARG5, then the instruction. The result comes back in RETURN.

API

curl https://api.syscall.sh/v2/syscalls/x64/read

Any kernel release, diffs between releases and more in the API docs.

Syscall tables across kernel versions

Entries get added and, rarely, removed between releases. Each architecture page has a kernel selector, and its JSON download records when each entry first appeared (since) and when it was dropped (removed_in).

Removed entries stay visible: pick "all, with removed" in the kernel selector and each dropped syscall is marked with the release that dropped it.

Where the data comes from

Everything on this site is read from the kernel source itself. For each architecture, the generator walks the syscall table and the SYSCALL_DEFINE macros of every mainline release it scans, so these are the numbers the kernel actually dispatches on.

It also records each architecture's calling convention, the instruction that enters the kernel, so every syscall table shows exactly where the number and the arguments go.

A syscall whose since equals the first release scanned for its architecture was already there back then, and may be much older.

Descriptions and full history

The short descriptions come from the Linux man pages project, and the io_uring ones from liburing. Whenever the data changes, the site is rebuilt from the syscall API.
